lessons.title: 2. DOM & Event Fundamentals
lessons.description: The textContent property represents the text content of a DOM node. Implement `createButton(text)` as an arrow function that returns an object modelling a <button> element: { tag: 'button', textContent: text, disabled: false }. Export { createButton }. The test checks all three fields.

tests.name: test_create_button

learning_objectives: Model DOM element state as plain JavaScript objects
Use textContent as the DOM API defines it
Return object literals from arrow functions

source.name: MDN Web Docs — Node.textContent — 'represents the text content of the node and its descendants'

exercises.question: In `const createButton = (text) => { tag: 'button' }` the braces hand back that object, so an arrow function never needs parentheses around a returned object literal.
exercises.explanation: With braces, `{` opens the function body, so `tag: 'button'` is a labelled statement and the function returns undefined. Wrapping the object in parentheses - `=> ({ tag: 'button' })` - is what makes it the value handed back.
